goals.title: hyp prints the /goal prompt for any Goal from its log, and warns when a Goal's constraints block is unusable
goals.body:
Builds #113: hyp prompt prints the /goal prompt for any Goal from the log, and hyp add goal warns about a constraints block no prompt could use. The candidate is a hyp commit; go test on its base and on the candidate is the instrument. Constraints live in the Goal body under three headings and no typed field is added (owner, 2026-11-11). A prompt may narrow them, never widen them. Out of scope: what a commit-candidate Goal needs from hyp (#114), one root store versus one per topic, and matching run 6's prompt (a placeholder issue).

May change: this repository, as commits on one local branch
May change: the texts the change makes wrong, by directory: skills/, docs/, AGENTS.md, README.md, including a skill description that names only one kind of Goal
Read only: investigations/checkpoint-store and investigations/checkpoint-store-design
Never: open or merge a PR
Never: replace the installed hyp binary; build to a temporary path
Never: edit a Goal or an event already in a log
lines: [P] For a Goal whose body ends in a valid constraints block, `hyp prompt G --actor A` exits 0 and prints in order: the store path; the actor; the Goal id; the skill name hyp-goal-run; the stop clauses (the runner owes nothing; N Results recorded under the actor, non-retracted and on this Goal, N from --experiments, default 5; you cannot take the next step honestly and say why); the block, line for line in body order. --branch and --pr each add one clause after the block. Two runs over one log print identical bytes.

[P] Baseline run-5-prompt.txt, sha256 840d813d6f8e6b0c1502f3d629fc091b551dd90e5f823e5190ee35b055d7e3a3. On a synthetic store whose Goal has checkpoint-store:G-D1CH1R's title and lines and a body ending in a block of run 5's constraint lines, the output matches the baseline clause for clause and differs from it only in: actor, owner answer, branch, PR, commit, the run's own plan; the dropped add-rival-Hypotheses clause; Results for Experiments in the count clause; and run 5's Treat-as-legacy sentence, which prints as its Read only: line.

[N] `hyp prompt` exits 1, with a message naming the rule and nothing on stdout, for an unknown id, a node that is not a Goal, and a Goal body without a valid block. A valid block starts at the first line that begins at column 0 with May change:, Read only: or Never:, runs to the end of the body, holds all three headings, and every non-empty line in it starts at column 0 with one. A line of spaces, a tab or a lone carriage return is not empty.

[N] `hyp add goal` warns (a warn: line on stderr, exit 0, naming the rule) for exactly the bodies the previous line makes `hyp prompt` refuse, a body with no heading included. It never refuses the add, and a log holding such a body replays with `hyp check` reporting 0 errors.

[N] `hyp prompt` exits 2 for an --actor outside the replay-spec name pattern or missing; a --branch that is empty, starts with -, or has a character outside A-Za-z0-9._/-; and a --pr or --experiments that is not a positive integer.

[P] The output depends only on the merged projection. In a two-Goal store, `hyp prompt G-a` names only G-a's id and block and points to `hyp status G-a`; with the Goal's add and its checkpoints in two actors' files it prints the same bytes as when the events share one file.
[P] For a Goal that is complete, or whose OWED already says the runner owes nothing, `hyp prompt` still prints and exits 0.
[N] With no store (.tree/events) at or above the working directory, `hyp prompt` exits 3 and prints nothing on stdout.
